zebralogic.title: Interpret adjacency and ordering clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: Handle spatial clues in three distinct ways: (a) "directly left/right of" – enforce immediate adjacency; (b) "somewhere left/right of" – enforce ordering inequality; (c) "next to each other" – enforce adjacency without direction.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue describes the relative positions of two attribute values.
zebralogic.example: Treating a "directly left of" clue as merely "somewhere left of", allowing the two houses to be non‑adjacent.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says "N houses between X and Y", enforce that exactly N houses separate X and Y, i.e., the absolute difference of their positions equals N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a specific number of houses between two attributes.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "two houses between" as a distance of two positions instead of three.

zebralogic.title: Bind equivalence clues to the same house
zebralogic.principle: If a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., "X is Y" or "the person whose child is named X is the person who loves Y"), enforce that they belong to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue directly states that two attributes refer to the same entity.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring a clue that says "the person's child is named Alice is the person who loves cooking", treating the child and the cooking hobby as unrelated.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say X is somewhere left/right of Y impose only an ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(X) > pos(Y)), not adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the phrasing "somewhere left of" or "somewhere right of".
zebralogic.example: Treating "somewhere left of" as requiring X to be immediately left of Y, violating the intended flexibility.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from a specific house (e.g., "Peter is not in the fifth house"), remove that house from the attribute's possible positions.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains a negative placement.
zebralogic.example: Failing to exclude "Peter" from house 5 after a clue states he is not there, allowing an illegal placement.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses; after assigning a value, eliminate it from the possibilities of the remaining houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Continuously, after any assignment or reduction of possibilities.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same sport to two different houses, breaking the one‑per‑category rule.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: When producing the final grid, copy each attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem statement, preserving capitalization and spelling.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During the construction of the output JSON.
zebralogic.example: Changing "Alice" to "alice" or "Volleyball" to "volleyball" in the answer.

zebralogic.title: Make forced assignments when only one candidate remains
zebralogic.principle: If after applying all constraints a house (or an attribute) has exactly one possible remaining value, assign it immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a domain collapses to a single option.
zebralogic.example: Leaving a house with only one possible sport unfilled, causing later contradictions.

zebralogic.title: Disambiguate overlapping attribute values using clue context
zebralogic.principle: When a value appears in more than one attribute category, use the surrounding words in the clue to decide which category is intended.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When parsing any clue that mentions a value that could belong to multiple categories.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "cat lover" as referring to the Pet category instead of the Animal category.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model forgets that 'N houses between' counts the houses in between, not the total gap.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Add one to the stated number when computing the absolute position difference.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats the attributes independently, missing the implied equality.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue equates two attributes, immediately link their positions.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model does not keep a global record of which values have already been used.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Maintain a set of used values for each category and remove them from other houses' possibilities.

zebralogic.description: Altering attribute values (spelling/casing) instead of copying them verbatim
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model normalizes text or forgets to preserve the original formatting.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy each value exactly as it appears in the problem when writing the output.
